keyVerseText: Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: LORD, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb דָּאַב (dâʼab) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the experience of mourning or sorrow, with an emphasis on a deep internal weakening or languishing. Unlike the general English terms 'mourn' or 'sorrow,' its root sense includes the physical and emotional sense of becoming faint or pining away, reflecting a profound, embodied response to distress. This layered meaning enriches the understanding of sorrow as not merely an emotional state but a condition that affects the whole person.
usageInScripture: The word דָּאַב appears three times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently conveying sorrow or mourning. Its translations include 'mourneth,' 'and they shall not sorrow,' and 'every sorrowful,' showing a range from personal lament to communal or future absence of sorrow. This consistency highlights the word's core meaning of deep grief or distress, with occasional nuance toward the cessation of such sorrow, as seen in the promise that the ransomed will no longer pine away.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding דָּאַב as a term that encompasses both emotional and physical anguish deepens our grasp of human suffering in Scripture and the Christian life. It reminds believers that sorrow is not merely a mental state but can affect the whole being, pointing to the brokenness of the fallen world. Yet, the scriptural usage also hints at hope, where sorrow will cease for God's people, reflecting the redemptive work of Christ who bears our griefs and offers restoration. Thus, this word invites believers to bring their deepest pains to God, who understands and ultimately promises deliverance from mourning.
keyVerseReflection: In Psalms 88:9, 'Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: LORD, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee,' the use of דָּאַב conveys a sorrow so intense that it visibly affects the psalmist's very eyes, symbolizing deep and persistent grief. This word underscores the psalmist's earnest and continual appeal to God amid suffering, highlighting the raw emotional and physical reality of lament and the faithful dependence on the Lord in times of distress.
